issue.title: ToolRun retention never selects quarantined runs.sqlite.corrupt-* stores, so they accumulate forever under sase_home()/tools
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-135.7 (epic sase-135, "Named tools and the foreground ToolRun ledger") as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note; filed by the sase-135 land agent on 2026-09-20.

When the ToolRun store detects a corrupt SQLite database it quarantines the file by renaming it to `runs.sqlite.corrupt-*` under `sase_home()/tools/` and starts a fresh store. Nothing ever removes those quarantined files.

The epic's plan lists quarantined stores under retention, but the implementation in sase-core's `tool_run` retention only selects retained log files, event files, and projection rows. A quarantined store matches none of those selectors, so `sase disk reap` neither previews nor deletes one, and `sase disk list` accounts for the bytes without offering a way to reclaim them. Each corruption event therefore leaves a permanent copy of the whole store behind.

Remediation: extend retention selection in `../sase-core/crates/sase_core/src/tool_run/` to include quarantined stores under an explicit horizon, expose them through the existing preview/apply retention report so `sase disk reap` can show and reclaim them, and keep the honest physical-byte accounting DoD-9 requires. Per the Rust core backend boundary, the selection logic belongs in sase-core; `src/sase/core/disk_footprint_reap_tool_run.py` stays a thin adapter.

task_type_fields.impact: Every ToolRun store corruption permanently leaks a full copy of the store. On a busy host the ledger reaches hundreds of MB, so repeated corruption silently consumes disk that the tool_run_retention owner reports but cannot reclaim.
task_type_fields.location: ../sase-core/crates/sase_core/src/tool_run/store.rs (retention selection); surfaced through src/sase/core/disk_footprint_reap_tool_run.py and src/sase/core/disk_footprint_inventory.py (owner tool_run_retention)
task_type_fields.repro: Corrupt an isolated ToolRun store so the next sase tool command quarantines it (truncate or overwrite sase_home()/tools/runs.sqlite with garbage, then run 'sase tool runs'). Confirm a runs.sqlite.corrupt-* file now exists beside it. Run 'sase disk reap --owner tool_run_retention' (preview) and then apply: the quarantined file is never listed and never deleted, at any horizon.

payload.entry: Fixed by phase sase-14n.10: sase-core retention now selects runs.sqlite.corrupt-* siblings older than the log_days horizon (age from filename quarantine nanos) as kind=quarantined_store through preview/apply, with young/unreadable bytes kept in retained_bytes. Verified: cargo test -p sase_core --lib tool_run:: 30 passed (2 new); pytest tests/tool/test_retention_files.py 3 passed (new reap preview+reclaim test: 64B reclaimed, live store intact); recorded just check 44230 passed, only failures the 2 pre-existing sase-13o queue_weight nodes.
